functions.name: ABS
functions.doc: Absolute value of n. The result has the same numeric datatype as the argument.

functions.name: ACOS
functions.doc: Arc cosine of n in radians (0 to pi). n must lie between -1 and 1. Returns BINARY_DOUBLE for binary floating-point input, else NUMBER.

functions.name: ADD_MONTHS
functions.doc: Adds integer months (may be negative) to date. If date is the last day of its month, or the target month is shorter, the result is the last day of the target month.

functions.name: ANY_VALUE
functions.doc: Returns an arbitrary (nondeterministic) value of expr from the group, ignoring NULLs where possible. Handy for columns functionally dependent on GROUP BY keys. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: APPENDCHILDXML
functions.doc: Appends value_expr as the last child of nodes selected by XPath. Deprecated: use XQuery Update in XMLQUERY.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT
functions.doc: Approximate count, typically paired with APPROX_RANK in HAVING for top-N queries. 'MAX_ERROR' returns the error bound instead.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.doc: Approximate number of distinct non-NULL values; much faster than COUNT(DISTINCT) on large data with negligible error.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT_AGG
functions.doc: Merges APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT_DETAIL results to coarser groups, returning a new detail BLOB.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT_DETAIL
functions.doc: Returns a BLOB summarising approximate distinct counts that can be stored and later aggregated or converted with TO_APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT.

functions.name: APPROX_MEDIAN
functions.doc: Approximate median of a numeric or datetime expression. DETERMINISTIC gives repeatable results; the optional string returns accuracy metadata.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE
functions.doc: Approximate inverse distribution: APPROX_PERCENTILE(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col). Faster than PERCENTILE_CONT on large sets.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE_AGG
functions.doc: Merges APPROX_PERCENTILE_DETAIL results into higher-level aggregation detail.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE_DETAIL
functions.doc: Returns a BLOB of approximate percentile information for later use with TO_APPROX_PERCENTILE.

functions.name: APPROX_RANK
functions.doc: Approximate rank used in the HAVING clause of a query with APPROX_COUNT or APPROX_SUM for top-N per group.

functions.name: APPROX_SUM
functions.doc: Approximate sum for top-N style queries combined with APPROX_RANK. Values must be non-negative.

functions.name: ASCII
functions.doc: Decimal code, in the database character set, of the first character of char.

functions.name: ASCIISTR
functions.doc: Returns an ASCII version of char: non-ASCII characters become \xxxx UTF-16 escapes and backslashes are doubled.

functions.name: ASIN
functions.doc: Arc sine of n in radians (-pi/2 to pi/2). n must lie between -1 and 1.

functions.name: ATAN
functions.doc: Arc tangent of n in radians (-pi/2 to pi/2). Any numeric value is accepted.

functions.name: ATAN2
functions.doc: Arc tangent of n1/n2 in radians, using the signs of both arguments to choose the quadrant; result ranges from -pi to pi.

functions.name: AVG
functions.doc: Average of non-NULL values of expr. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: BFILENAME
functions.doc: Returns a BFILE locator for a file in a directory object, e.g. BFILENAME('DATA_DIR', 'img.png'). The directory name is case-sensitive.

functions.name: BIN_TO_NUM
functions.doc: Treats the arguments as bits (each 0 or 1, most significant first) and returns the number, e.g. BIN_TO_NUM(1,0,1) = 5.

functions.name: BIT_AND_AGG
functions.doc: Bitwise AND of all non-NULL integer values in the group.

functions.name: BIT_OR_AGG
functions.doc: Bitwise OR of all non-NULL integer values in the group.

functions.name: BIT_XOR_AGG
functions.doc: Bitwise XOR of all non-NULL integer values in the group.

functions.name: BITAND
functions.doc: Bitwise AND of two integer values (fractional parts are truncated). Commonly combined with DECODE to test flag bits.

functions.name: BOOLEAN_AND_AGG
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if every non-NULL boolean value in the group is TRUE.

functions.name: BOOLEAN_OR_AGG
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if at least one non-NULL boolean value in the group is TRUE.

functions.name: CARDINALITY
functions.doc: Number of elements in a nested table; NULL if the table is NULL or empty.

functions.name: CAST

signatures.doc: Converts a scalar value; the DEFAULT/fmt/nlsparam options exist since 12.2.
Builds a nested table or varray from the rows of a subquery.

functions.doc: Converts a value to another built-in or collection type, e.g. CAST(x AS VARCHAR2(30)). CAST(MULTISET(...)) turns query rows into a collection.

functions.name: CEIL

signatures.doc: Oracle 23ai: rounds a datetime up to the unit given by fmt (default DD).

functions.doc: Smallest integer greater than or equal to n. In 23ai it also accepts a datetime and rounds it up to a format unit.

functions.name: CHARTOROWID
functions.doc: Converts a string in extended rowid format to a ROWID value.

functions.name: CHECKSUM
functions.doc: Order-independent checksum over the values of expr in a group; useful to detect changes in table data.

functions.name: CHR

signatures.doc: Returns the character from the national character set.

functions.doc: Character whose binary code is n in the database character set. CHR(10) is a line feed, CHR(13) a carriage return.

functions.name: CLUSTER_DETAILS
functions.doc: XML string describing which attributes most influenced the cluster assignment. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: CLUSTER_DISTANCE
functions.doc: Distance from the row to the centroid of the given (or best) cluster. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: CLUSTER_ID
functions.doc: ID of the most probable cluster for the row. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: CLUSTER_PROBABILITY
functions.doc: Probability that the row belongs to the given (or best) cluster. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: CLUSTER_SET
functions.doc: Varray of (CLUSTER_ID, PROBABILITY) pairs for the row, limited by topN and cutoff. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: COALESCE
functions.doc: Returns the first non-NULL argument. Uses short-circuit evaluation; all arguments must be of compatible types (stricter than NVL).

functions.name: COLLATION
functions.doc: Name of the derived data-bound collation of a character expression, e.g. BINARY or USING_NLS_COMP.

functions.name: COLLECT
functions.doc: Builds a nested table from the values in the group. Usually wrapped in CAST(COLLECT(...) AS my_table_type).

functions.name: COLUMN_VALUE
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn naming the value of a scalar collection element when using TABLE(collection), or an XMLTABLE row without COLUMNS.

functions.name: COMPOSE
functions.doc: Returns char in Unicode NFC (fully composed) form, e.g. combining an a with a following accent code point into one character.

functions.name: CON_DBID_TO_ID
functions.doc: Returns the container ID (CON_ID) for a container DBID in a multitenant database.

functions.name: CON_GUID_TO_ID
functions.doc: Returns the container ID for a container GUID.

functions.name: CON_NAME_TO_ID
functions.doc: Returns the container ID for a container (PDB) name.

functions.name: CON_UID_TO_ID
functions.doc: Returns the container ID for a container UID.

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.doc: Concatenates exactly two strings, same as the || operator. Nest calls for more values. Unlike most functions, a NULL argument is treated as an empty string.

functions.name: CONNECT_BY_ISCYCLE
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn: 1 if the current row has a child that is also its ancestor. Requires CONNECT BY NOCYCLE.

functions.name: CONNECT_BY_ISLEAF
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn: 1 if the current row has no children in the CONNECT BY hierarchy, otherwise 0.

functions.name: CONVERT
functions.doc: Converts char from source_char_set (default the database charset) to dest_char_set, e.g. CONVERT(s, 'US7ASCII', 'WE8ISO8859P1').

functions.name: CORR
functions.doc: Pearson correlation coefficient of a set of number pairs, ignoring pairs with a NULL. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: CORR_K
functions.doc: Kendall's tau-b rank correlation; the optional keyword returns the coefficient (default) or a significance value.

functions.name: CORR_S
functions.doc: Spearman's rho rank correlation; the optional keyword returns the coefficient (default) or a significance value.

functions.name: COS
functions.doc: Cosine of n, where n is an angle in radians.

functions.name: COSH
functions.doc: Hyperbolic cosine of n.

functions.name: COSINE_DISTANCE
functions.doc: Cosine distance (1 - cosine similarity) between two vectors; shorthand for VECTOR_DISTANCE(..., COSINE).

functions.name: COUNT
functions.doc: COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(expr) counts rows where expr is not NULL. Never returns NULL. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: COVAR_POP
functions.doc: Population covariance of number pairs, ignoring pairs containing NULL. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: COVAR_SAMP
functions.doc: Sample covariance of number pairs, ignoring pairs containing NULL. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: CUME_DIST

signatures.doc: Analytic: CUME_DIST() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).
Aggregate: CUME_DIST(value) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col).

functions.doc: Cumulative distribution (0 < x <= 1) of a value within a group. Aggregate form uses WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...); analytic form OVER (ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: CURRENT_DATE
functions.doc: Current date and time in the session time zone, as a DATE. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

signatures.doc: Fractional-seconds precision 0-9 (default 6).

functions.doc: Current date and time in the session time zone as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE. Optional precision in parentheses.

functions.name: CV
functions.doc: In a MODEL rule, returns the current value of a dimension column referenced on the left side, e.g. s[ANY] = s[CV()] * 2.

functions.name: DBTIMEZONE
functions.doc: Database time zone as an offset (+hh:mi) or region name, as set at database creation or by ALTER DATABASE.

functions.name: DECODE
functions.doc: Compares expr with each search value and returns the matching result, or default (NULL if omitted). Unlike =, DECODE treats two NULLs as equal. SQL only.

functions.name: DECOMPOSE
functions.doc: Returns the Unicode decomposition of string: CANONICAL (default, NFD) or COMPATIBILITY (NFKD).

functions.name: DELETEXML
functions.doc: Removes the nodes matched by XPath and returns the result. Deprecated: use XQuery Update.

functions.name: DENSE_RANK

signatures.doc: Analytic: DENSE_RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).
Aggregate: DENSE_RANK(value) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col).

functions.doc: Rank of a row with no gaps after ties. Analytic: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...). Also used in KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST/LAST ...).

functions.name: DEPTH
functions.doc: Ancillary to UNDER_PATH/EQUALS_PATH in XML DB repository queries: returns the path depth for the matching condition.

functions.name: DEREF
functions.doc: Returns the object that a REF value points to.

functions.name: DOMAIN_CHECK
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the values satisfy both the datatype and the check constraints of the named data use case domain.

functions.name: DOMAIN_CHECK_TYPE
functions.doc: Returns TRUE if the values are compatible with the datatype of the named domain (constraints are not evaluated).

functions.name: DOMAIN_DISPLAY
functions.doc: Evaluates the DISPLAY expression of the domain associated with a column, for formatted presentation.

functions.name: DOMAIN_NAME
functions.doc: Fully qualified name of the domain associated with a column expression, or NULL.

functions.name: DOMAIN_ORDER
functions.doc: Evaluates the ORDER expression of the domain associated with a column, for domain-defined sorting.

functions.name: DUMP
functions.doc: Returns the internal datatype code, byte length and bytes of expr, e.g. Typ=1 Len=3: 97,98,99. return_fmt 16 gives hex; adding 1000 shows the charset.

functions.name: EMPTY_BLOB
functions.doc: Returns an empty BLOB locator for initializing a column or variable before writing to it; an empty LOB is not NULL.

functions.name: EMPTY_CLOB
functions.doc: Returns an empty CLOB/NCLOB locator for initializing a LOB before writing; an empty LOB is not NULL.

functions.name: EXISTSNODE
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the XPath selects at least one node, otherwise 0. Deprecated: use XMLEXISTS.

functions.name: EXP
functions.doc: e raised to the power n (e = 2.71828183...).

functions.name: EXTRACT

signatures.doc: Datetime/interval field extraction. TIMEZONE_REGION and TIMEZONE_ABBR return VARCHAR2.
Deprecated XML form: returns the XML fragment matched by XPath. Use XMLQUERY instead.

functions.doc: Returns one field of a datetime or interval value, e.g. EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date). HOUR/MINUTE/SECOND need a TIMESTAMP (on DATE they raise an error).

functions.name: EXTRACTVALUE
functions.doc: Returns the scalar text value of the single node matched by XPath. Deprecated: use XMLTABLE, XMLQUERY or XMLCAST.

functions.name: FEATURE_DETAILS
functions.doc: XML string describing the attributes that most influenced a feature value. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: FEATURE_ID
functions.doc: ID of the feature with the highest coefficient value for the row. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: FEATURE_SET
functions.doc: Varray of (FEATURE_ID, VALUE) pairs for the row. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: FEATURE_VALUE
functions.doc: Value of the given (or highest) feature for the row. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: FIRST

params: aggregate_function(expr) KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST ORDER BY expr [ASC|DESC] [NULLS FIRST|LAST])

functions.doc: Modifier of MIN/MAX/SUM/AVG/COUNT etc.: aggregates only the rows ranked first by the ORDER BY, e.g. MAX(sal) KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST ORDER BY hiredate). Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: FIRST_VALUE
functions.doc: First value in the ordered window: FIRST_VALUE(x) [IGNORE NULLS] OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ... [frame]).

functions.name: FLOOR

signatures.doc: Oracle 23ai: truncates a datetime down to the unit given by fmt (default DD).

functions.doc: Largest integer less than or equal to n. In 23ai it also accepts a datetime and rounds it down to a format unit.

functions.name: FROM_TZ
functions.doc: Attaches a time zone to a TIMESTAMP, producing TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE. time_zone_value is like '+05:30' or 'Europe/Berlin'.

functions.name: FROM_VECTOR
functions.doc: Converts a VECTOR value to its textual representation.

functions.name: GREATEST
functions.doc: Largest value in the list. The first argument determines the comparison type; returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: GROUP_ID
functions.doc: Distinguishes duplicate groups produced by a GROUP BY with repeated grouping sets: 0 for the first copy, 1.. for duplicates.

functions.name: GROUPING
functions.doc: Returns 1 when expr is NULL because the row is a ROLLUP/CUBE/GROUPING SETS super-aggregate, otherwise 0.

functions.name: GROUPING_ID
functions.doc: Bit vector of GROUPING values for the listed columns, identifying the grouping level of each row in ROLLUP/CUBE results.

functions.name: HEXTORAW
functions.doc: Converts a string of hexadecimal digits to a RAW value, e.g. HEXTORAW('7D').

functions.name: INITCAP
functions.doc: Returns char with the first letter of each word upper-case and the rest lower-case. Words are delimited by white space or non-alphanumeric characters.

functions.name: INNER_PRODUCT
functions.doc: Dot product of two vectors (larger means more similar). Note VECTOR_DISTANCE DOT returns its negation.

functions.name: INSERTCHILDXML
functions.doc: Inserts child elements or attributes under nodes matched by XPath. Deprecated: use XQuery Update.

functions.name: INSERTCHILDXMLAFTER
functions.doc: Inserts XML after existing children identified by child_expr under the XPath target. Deprecated.

functions.name: INSERTCHILDXMLBEFORE
functions.doc: Inserts XML before existing children identified by child_expr under the XPath target. Deprecated.

functions.name: INSERTXMLAFTER
functions.doc: Inserts XML immediately after the nodes matched by XPath. Deprecated: use XQuery Update.

functions.name: INSERTXMLBEFORE
functions.doc: Inserts XML immediately before the nodes matched by XPath. Deprecated: use XQuery Update.

functions.name: INSTR
functions.doc: Position of the occurrence-th match of substring in string, starting at position (negative counts from the end and searches backward). Returns 0 if not found.

functions.name: INSTR2
functions.doc: Like INSTR but counts UCS2 code points.

functions.name: INSTR4
functions.doc: Like INSTR but counts UCS4 code points.

functions.name: INSTRB
functions.doc: Like INSTR but positions are measured in bytes rather than characters.

functions.name: INSTRC
functions.doc: Like INSTR but counts Unicode complete characters.

functions.name: ITERATION_NUMBER
functions.doc: In MODEL ... ITERATE, the 0-based number of the current iteration.

functions.name: JSON
functions.doc: Constructor that parses textual JSON (or a binary value) into the native JSON datatype.

functions.name: JSON_ARRAY
functions.doc: Builds a JSON array from the arguments (or from a single-column subquery). NULL elements are omitted by default (ABSENT ON NULL).

functions.name: JSON_ARRAYAGG
functions.doc: Aggregates the values in a group into a single JSON array. NULLs are omitted by default (ABSENT ON NULL).

functions.name: JSON_DATAGUIDE
functions.doc: Computes a data guide (JSON schema-like summary of fields and types) over a set of JSON documents.

functions.name: JSON_EQUAL
functions.doc: Condition that is true when two JSON values are semantically equal, ignoring member order and insignificant whitespace.

functions.name: JSON_EXISTS
functions.doc: Condition testing whether a SQL/JSON path selects anything, e.g. WHERE JSON_EXISTS(doc, '$.items?(@.qty > 5)'). Supports filter expressions.

functions.name: JSON_MERGEPATCH
functions.doc: Applies an RFC 7396 merge patch to a JSON document: members are added or replaced, and members patched with null are removed.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECT
functions.doc: Builds a JSON object from key/value pairs, e.g. JSON_OBJECT('id' VALUE id, 'name' VALUE name). JSON_OBJECT(*) uses all columns. NULL ON NULL is the default.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECTAGG
functions.doc: Aggregates key/value pairs from a group into a single JSON object. NULL values are included by default (NULL ON NULL).

functions.name: JSON_QUERY
functions.doc: Returns a JSON fragment (object or array) selected by a path. Use a WRAPPER clause to return scalars or multiple matches as an array.

functions.name: JSON_SCALAR
functions.doc: Converts a SQL scalar value (number, string, date, timestamp, raw...) to a JSON scalar of the native JSON type.

functions.name: JSON_SERIALIZE
functions.doc: Converts JSON (text, binary OSON or native JSON) to textual JSON, with options to pretty-print, escape non-ASCII, or sort keys.

functions.name: JSON_TABLE

params: COLUMNS (col_name type PATH '$.x' | col_name FOR ORDINALITY | NESTED PATH '$.arr[*]' COLUMNS (...), ...)

functions.doc: Projects JSON data as relational rows and columns in the FROM clause: FROM t, JSON_TABLE(t.doc, '$.items[*]' COLUMNS (...)). NESTED PATH unnests arrays.

functions.name: JSON_TEXTCONTAINS
functions.doc: Condition that does a full-text search in JSON data at a path; requires a JSON search index.

functions.name: JSON_TRANSFORM
functions.doc: Modifies a JSON document with a list of operations, e.g. JSON_TRANSFORM(doc, SET '$.status' = 'done', REMOVE '$.tmp'). Usable in UPDATE or SELECT.

functions.name: JSON_VALUE
functions.doc: Extracts a single SQL scalar from JSON by path, e.g. JSON_VALUE(doc, '$.price' RETURNING NUMBER). Errors return NULL by default (NULL ON ERROR).

functions.name: KURTOSIS_POP
functions.doc: Population kurtosis (tailedness) of the values in the group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: KURTOSIS_SAMP
functions.doc: Sample kurtosis of the values in the group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: L1_DISTANCE
functions.doc: Manhattan (L1) distance between two vectors.

functions.name: L2_DISTANCE
functions.doc: Euclidean (L2) distance between two vectors.

functions.name: LAG
functions.doc: Value from a row offset rows (default 1) before the current one: LAG(x, 1, 0) [IGNORE NULLS] OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...). default replaces a missing row.

functions.name: LAST

params: aggregate_function(expr) KEEP (DENSE_RANK LAST ORDER BY expr [ASC|DESC] [NULLS FIRST|LAST])

functions.doc: Modifier of an aggregate: aggregates only the rows ranked last by the ORDER BY, e.g. MIN(sal) KEEP (DENSE_RANK LAST ORDER BY hiredate). Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: LAST_DAY
functions.doc: Date of the last day of the month containing date; the time portion is kept.

functions.name: LAST_VALUE
functions.doc: Last value in the window frame. With ORDER BY the default frame ends at the current row, so add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.

functions.name: LEAD
functions.doc: Value from a row offset rows (default 1) after the current one: LEAD(x) [IGNORE NULLS] OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: LEAST
functions.doc: Smallest value in the list. The first argument determines the comparison type; returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: LENGTH
functions.doc: Number of characters in char. Returns NULL (not 0) for NULL or an empty string, since Oracle treats empty strings as NULL.

functions.name: LENGTH2
functions.doc: Length of char in UCS2 code points.

functions.name: LENGTH4
functions.doc: Length of char in UCS4 code points.

functions.name: LENGTHB
functions.doc: Length of char in bytes. Not valid for multibyte CLOB/NCLOB values.

functions.name: LENGTHC
functions.doc: Length of char in Unicode complete characters.

functions.name: LEVEL
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn in hierarchical (CONNECT BY) queries: 1 for root rows, 2 for their children, etc. Also used for row generators: CONNECT BY LEVEL <= n.

functions.name: LISTAGG

params: [ON OVERFLOW ERROR | ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE ['indicator'] [WITH|WITHOUT COUNT]]

functions.doc: Concatenates values in a group: LISTAGG(col, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col). ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE avoids ORA-01489; DISTINCT since 19c. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: LN
functions.doc: Natural logarithm of n; n must be greater than 0.

functions.name: LNNVL
functions.doc: Condition that is true when the given condition is false or unknown (NULL), e.g. WHERE LNNVL(commission > 0). Only simple conditions are allowed.

functions.name: LOCALTIMESTAMP

signatures.doc: Fractional-seconds precision 0-9 (default 6).

functions.doc: Current date and time in the session time zone as TIMESTAMP (no time zone). Differs from CURRENT_TIMESTAMP only in the datatype.

functions.name: LOG
functions.doc: Logarithm of n in the given base. Note the order: LOG(base, n). base must be positive and not 1; n must be positive.

functions.name: LOWER
functions.doc: Returns char with all letters in lower case.

functions.name: LPAD
functions.doc: Left-pads expr1 to n display characters using expr2 (default a single blank). If expr1 is longer than n, it is cut to n.

functions.name: LTRIM
functions.doc: Removes from the left of char every character that appears in set (default a single blank), stopping at the first character not in set.

functions.name: MAKE_REF
functions.doc: Builds a REF to a row of an object view or object table with a primary-key-based object identifier.

functions.name: MAX
functions.doc: Maximum value of expr in the group, ignoring NULLs. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: MEDIAN
functions.doc: Median (interpolated middle value) of a numeric or datetime expression, ignoring NULLs. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: MIN
functions.doc: Minimum value of expr in the group, ignoring NULLs. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: MOD
functions.doc: Remainder of n2 divided by n1; the result takes the sign of n2. Returns n2 when n1 is 0.

functions.name: MONTHS_BETWEEN
functions.doc: Months between date1 and date2; positive if date1 is later. Whole number when days match or both are month-ends, else fractional based on a 31-day month.

functions.name: NANVL
functions.doc: Returns n1 when n2 is NaN (not a number), otherwise n2. Meaningful only for BINARY_FLOAT and BINARY_DOUBLE values.

functions.name: NCHR
functions.doc: Character whose binary code is number in the national character set. Equivalent to CHR(n USING NCHAR_CS).

functions.name: NEW_TIME
functions.doc: Converts a date from timezone1 to timezone2. Supports only a few North American abbreviations (AST, CST, EST, GMT, PST...); prefer FROM_TZ/AT TIME ZONE.

functions.name: NEXT_DAY
functions.doc: Date of the first weekday named by char that is later than date, e.g. NEXT_DAY(SYSDATE, 'MONDAY'). The day name uses the session date language.

functions.name: NLS_CHARSET_DECL_LEN
functions.doc: Declaration length, in characters, of an NCHAR column of byte_count bytes in the given character set.

functions.name: NLS_CHARSET_ID
functions.doc: Character set ID for a character set name; 'CHAR_CS' and 'NCHAR_CS' give the database and national sets.

functions.name: NLS_CHARSET_NAME
functions.doc: Character set name for a character set ID.

functions.name: NLS_COLLATION_ID
functions.doc: Numeric collation ID for a collation name.

functions.name: NLS_COLLATION_NAME
functions.doc: Collation name for a collation ID; flag 'S' (default) returns the short form, 'L' the long form.

functions.name: NLS_INITCAP
functions.doc: INITCAP with linguistic rules; nlsparam has the form 'NLS_SORT = sort_name' to handle language-specific casing.

functions.name: NLS_LOWER
functions.doc: LOWER with linguistic rules; nlsparam has the form 'NLS_SORT = sort_name'.

functions.name: NLS_UPPER
functions.doc: UPPER with linguistic rules; nlsparam has the form 'NLS_SORT = sort_name' (e.g. XGERMAN maps sharp s to SS).

functions.name: NLSSORT
functions.doc: Returns the collation key used to sort char under a linguistic sort, e.g. NLSSORT(name, 'NLS_SORT = GERMAN'). Useful in ORDER BY and comparisons.

functions.name: NTH_VALUE
functions.doc: n-th value in the window: NTH_VALUE(x, 2) [FROM FIRST|LAST] [RESPECT|IGNORE NULLS] OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ... frame).

functions.name: NTILE
functions.doc: Divides ordered rows into expr buckets numbered 1..expr: NTILE(4) OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...). Earlier buckets get any extra rows.

functions.name: NULLIF
functions.doc: Returns NULL if expr1 equals expr2, otherwise expr1. expr1 cannot be the literal NULL.

functions.name: NUMTODSINTERVAL
functions.doc: Converts n to an INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND in the given unit, e.g. NUMTODSINTERVAL(90, 'MINUTE'). The unit is case-insensitive.

functions.name: NUMTOYMINTERVAL
functions.doc: Converts n to an INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH in the given unit, e.g. NUMTOYMINTERVAL(18, 'MONTH').

functions.name: NVL
functions.doc: Returns expr2 when expr1 is NULL, otherwise expr1. expr2 is converted to the type of expr1; both arguments are always evaluated.

functions.name: NVL2
functions.doc: Returns expr2 if expr1 is not NULL, otherwise expr3.

functions.name: OBJECT_ID
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn returning the object identifier of a row in an object table or object view.

functions.name: OBJECT_VALUE
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn returning the object instance of a row in an object table or XMLType table.

functions.name: ORA_DM_PARTITION_NAME
functions.doc: Name of the model partition that would score the row in a partitioned mining model. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: ORA_DST_AFFECTED
functions.doc: Used while upgrading the time zone file: returns 1 if the value is affected by the new DST rules (overlap, gap or zone change), else 0.

functions.name: ORA_DST_CONVERT
functions.doc: Used during a time zone file upgrade to convert a value under the new DST rules, optionally raising errors for overlapping or non-existing times.

functions.name: ORA_DST_ERROR
functions.doc: Used during a time zone file upgrade: returns 0 if OK, or ORA-01878 / ORA-01883 codes for non-existing or overlapping times.

functions.name: ORA_HASH
functions.doc: Computes a hash value for expr in the range 0..max_bucket (default 4294967295). Useful for sampling or bucketing; not cryptographic.

functions.name: ORA_INVOKING_USER
functions.doc: Name of the user who invoked the current statement or view; with BEQUEATH CURRENT_USER views it sees through definer layers.

functions.name: ORA_INVOKING_USERID
functions.doc: Numeric ID of the user who invoked the current statement or view.

functions.name: ORA_ROWSCN
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn: upper-bound SCN of the last change to the row (block level unless the table uses ROWDEPENDENCIES).

functions.name: PATH
functions.doc: Ancillary to UNDER_PATH/EQUALS_PATH: returns the relative repository path of the resource matched by the condition.

functions.name: PERCENT_RANK

signatures.doc: Analytic: PERCENT_RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).
Aggregate: PERCENT_RANK(value) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col).

functions.doc: Relative rank (rank-1)/(rows-1), from 0 to 1. Aggregate form uses WITHIN GROUP; analytic form OVER (ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.doc: Continuous percentile with interpolation: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY sal). expr is a fraction 0-1. Analytic with OVER (PARTITION BY ...).

functions.name: PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.doc: Discrete percentile: returns an actual value from the set, PERCENTILE_DISC(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col). Analytic with OVER (PARTITION BY ...).

functions.name: POWER
functions.doc: n2 raised to the power n1. If n2 is negative, n1 must be an integer.

functions.name: POWERMULTISET
functions.doc: Returns a nested table of nested tables containing all non-empty subsets of the input nested table.

functions.name: POWERMULTISET_BY_CARDINALITY
functions.doc: Returns all subsets of the input nested table that have exactly the given number of elements.

functions.name: PREDICTION
functions.doc: Best prediction (class or regression value) for the row from a mining model. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: PREDICTION_BOUNDS
functions.doc: Object with LOWER and UPPER confidence bounds for a GLM model prediction. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: PREDICTION_COST
functions.doc: Cost of the best or given prediction using a cost matrix. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: PREDICTION_DETAILS
functions.doc: XML string describing the attributes that most influenced the prediction. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: PREDICTION_PROBABILITY
functions.doc: Probability of the best or given class prediction for the row. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: PREDICTION_SET
functions.doc: Varray of (PREDICTION, PROBABILITY[, COST]) objects for the row. Analytic form: OVER (mining_analytic_clause).

functions.name: PRESENTNNV
functions.doc: In a MODEL clause, returns expr1 if the cell existed before evaluation and is not NULL, otherwise expr2.

functions.name: PRESENTV
functions.doc: In a MODEL clause, returns expr1 if the cell existed before evaluation (even if NULL), otherwise expr2.

functions.name: PREVIOUS
functions.doc: In MODEL ... ITERATE ... UNTIL, the value of a cell at the start of the current iteration.

functions.name: RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR
functions.doc: PL/SQL procedure (not a function): raises a user-defined error with a code from -20000 to -20999. keep_errors TRUE appends to the error stack.

functions.name: RANK

signatures.doc: Analytic: RANK() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...).
Aggregate: RANK(value) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col).

functions.doc: Rank of a row with gaps after ties (1,1,3). Analytic: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...); aggregate: RANK(v) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...).

functions.name: RATIO_TO_REPORT
functions.doc: Ratio of a value to the sum over the window: RATIO_TO_REPORT(sal) OVER ([PARTITION BY dept]). ORDER BY and frames are not allowed.

functions.name: RAWTOHEX
functions.doc: Converts a RAW value to a string of hexadecimal digits.

functions.name: RAWTONHEX
functions.doc: Converts a RAW value to hexadecimal digits in the national character set.

functions.name: REF
functions.doc: Returns a REF to the row object bound to a table alias of an object table or view.

functions.name: REFTOHEX
functions.doc: Converts a REF value to its hexadecimal string form.

functions.name: REGEXP_COUNT
functions.doc: Number of times a POSIX regular expression matches in source_char, searching from position. match_param flags: i, c, n, m, x.

functions.name: REGEXP_INSTR
functions.doc: Position of a regex match; return_opt 0 gives the start of the match, 1 the position after it. subexpr selects a capture group. Returns 0 if no match.

functions.name: REGEXP_LIKE
functions.doc: Condition (usable in WHERE/CASE) that is true when source_char matches the regular expression. match_param: 'i' ignore case, 'c' case-sensitive, 'n', 'm', 'x'.

functions.name: REGEXP_REPLACE
functions.doc: Replaces regex matches with replace_string, which may use back-references \1..\9. occurrence 0 (default) replaces all matches.

functions.name: REGEXP_SUBSTR
functions.doc: Returns the substring matching a regular expression, or NULL. subexpr (0-9) returns a specific capture group instead of the whole match.

functions.name: REGR_AVGX
functions.doc: Average of the independent variable x in the linear regression. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_AVGY
functions.doc: Average of the dependent variable y in the linear regression. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_COUNT
functions.doc: Number of non-NULL (y, x) pairs used in the regression. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_INTERCEPT
functions.doc: y-intercept of the least-squares regression line. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_R2
functions.doc: Coefficient of determination (R squared) of the regression. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_SLOPE
functions.doc: Slope of the least-squares regression line. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_SXX
functions.doc: REGR_COUNT * VAR_POP(x): sum of squares of x deviations. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_SXY
functions.doc: REGR_COUNT * COVAR_POP(y, x): sum of products of deviations. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REGR_SYY
functions.doc: REGR_COUNT * VAR_POP(y): sum of squares of y deviations. Pairs with a NULL are ignored. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: REMAINDER
functions.doc: n2 minus n1 times the integer nearest n2/n1. Like MOD but uses ROUND instead of FLOOR, so the result can be negative.

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.doc: Replaces every occurrence of search_string in char with replacement_string. If replacement is omitted or NULL, the matches are removed.

functions.name: ROUND

signatures.doc: Rounds n to integer places right of the decimal point (negative rounds to the left). Default 0.
Rounds a date to the unit in fmt (e.g. YYYY, MM, DD, HH24, MI). Default DD (nearest day).

functions.doc: Rounds a number to a number of decimal places, or a datetime to a format unit. NUMBER rounds half away from zero; binary floats round half to even.

functions.name: ROW_NUMBER
functions.doc: Sequential number for each row starting at 1: ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...). Ties get distinct numbers; common for top-N per group.

functions.name: ROWID
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn giving the physical address of a row; the fastest way to access a single row. Can change after moves, exports or partition operations.

functions.name: ROWIDTOCHAR
functions.doc: Converts a ROWID to its 18-character string form.

functions.name: ROWIDTONCHAR
functions.doc: Converts a ROWID to its string form in the national character set.

functions.name: ROWNUM
functions.doc: Pseudocolumn numbering rows in the order they are returned, assigned before ORDER BY. ROWNUM > 1 never matches; filter in an outer query for top-N.

functions.name: RPAD
functions.doc: Right-pads expr1 to n display characters using expr2 (default a single blank). If expr1 is longer than n, it is cut to n.

functions.name: RTRIM
functions.doc: Removes from the right of char every character that appears in set (default a single blank).

functions.name: SCN_TO_TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Approximate timestamp at which a system change number was generated. Only works for recent SCNs retained by the database (typically days).

functions.name: SESSIONTIMEZONE
functions.doc: Session time zone as an offset or region name, set by ALTER SESSION SET TIME_ZONE or the client.

functions.name: SET
functions.doc: Removes duplicate elements from a nested table and returns the result.

functions.name: SIGN
functions.doc: Returns -1, 0 or 1 depending on whether n is negative, zero or positive. For binary floats, returns -1 for negative values and 1 otherwise (incl. NaN).

functions.name: SIN
functions.doc: Sine of n, where n is an angle in radians.

functions.name: SINH
functions.doc: Hyperbolic sine of n.

functions.name: SKEWNESS_POP
functions.doc: Population skewness (asymmetry) of the values in the group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: SKEWNESS_SAMP
functions.doc: Sample skewness of the values in the group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: SOUNDEX
functions.doc: Phonetic code for char (letter plus three digits) so that similar-sounding English words compare equal.

functions.name: SQLCODE
functions.doc: PL/SQL only: error number of the most recent exception (0 if none, +100 for NO_DATA_FOUND, 1 for user-defined). Cannot be used directly in SQL.

functions.name: SQLERRM
functions.doc: PL/SQL only: message for the current exception, or for error_number. Prefer DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_STACK for long stacks. Not usable in SQL.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.doc: Square root of n. n must not be negative for NUMBER; for binary floats a negative argument yields NaN.

functions.name: STANDARD_HASH
functions.doc: Cryptographic hash of expr using the given algorithm (default SHA1), e.g. STANDARD_HASH(pwd, 'SHA256'). LOB types are not supported.

functions.name: STATS_BINOMIAL_TEST
functions.doc: Exact binomial test of whether the proportion of expr1 values equal to expr2 differs from p.

functions.name: STATS_CROSSTAB
functions.doc: Crosstab analysis of two nominal variables: chi-square statistics and association measures. Default CHISQ_SIG.

functions.name: STATS_F_TEST
functions.doc: F-test of whether two group variances differ significantly; expr1 is the grouping column. Default TWO_SIDED_SIG.

functions.name: STATS_KS_TEST
functions.doc: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of whether two samples come from the same distribution. Default SIG.

functions.name: STATS_MODE
functions.doc: Most frequent value in the group; if several tie, one of them is returned.

functions.name: STATS_MW_TEST
functions.doc: Mann-Whitney U test comparing two independent samples without assuming normality. Default TWO_SIDED_SIG.

functions.name: STATS_ONE_WAY_ANOVA
functions.doc: One-way analysis of variance across groups defined by expr1. Default SIG.

functions.name: STATS_T_TEST_INDEP
functions.doc: Two-sample t-test with pooled (equal) variances. Default TWO_SIDED_SIG.

functions.name: STATS_T_TEST_INDEPU
functions.doc: Two-sample t-test with unequal variances (Welch). Default TWO_SIDED_SIG.

functions.name: STATS_T_TEST_ONE
functions.doc: One-sample t-test of whether the mean of expr1 differs from expr2 (default 0).

functions.name: STATS_T_TEST_PAIRED
functions.doc: Paired t-test of whether the mean difference between expr1 and expr2 is zero.

functions.name: STATS_WSR_TEST
functions.doc: Wilcoxon signed-ranks test on paired samples. Default TWO_SIDED_SIG.

functions.name: STDDEV
functions.doc: Sample standard deviation; returns 0 (not NULL) for a single-row group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: STDDEV_POP
functions.doc: Population standard deviation (square root of VAR_POP). Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: STDDEV_SAMP
functions.doc: Cumulative sample standard deviation; returns NULL for a single-row group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: SUBSTR
functions.doc: Portion of char starting at position (1-based; 0 is treated as 1; negative counts from the end), substring_length characters long or to the end if omitted.

functions.name: SUBSTR2
functions.doc: Like SUBSTR but counts UCS2 code points.

functions.name: SUBSTR4
functions.doc: Like SUBSTR but counts UCS4 code points.

functions.name: SUBSTRB
functions.doc: Like SUBSTR but position and length are measured in bytes.

functions.name: SUBSTRC
functions.doc: Like SUBSTR but counts Unicode complete characters.

functions.name: SUM
functions.doc: Sum of non-NULL values of expr; NULL if all values are NULL. Running totals via SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY ...). Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH
functions.doc: In a CONNECT BY query, returns the path of column values from the root to the current row, each preceded by char, e.g. SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH(name, '/').

functions.name: SYS_CONTEXT
functions.doc: Value of an application context attribute, e.g. SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'SESSION_USER'). USERENV exposes session info; length defaults to 256 (max 4000).

functions.name: SYS_DBURIGEN
functions.doc: Builds a DBURIType URL pointing to a database column or row; append 'text()' to get the text value without XML markup.

functions.name: SYS_EXTRACT_UTC
functions.doc: Converts a timestamp with time zone to the equivalent UTC TIMESTAMP. If no zone is present, the session time zone is assumed.

functions.name: SYS_GUID
functions.doc: Generates a globally unique 16-byte RAW identifier; often used as a default key value. Use RAWTOHEX for display.

functions.name: SYS_TYPEID
functions.doc: Returns the type ID of the most specific type of an object instance (for substitutable columns).

functions.name: SYS_XMLAGG
functions.doc: Aggregates XML documents or fragments into a single document wrapped in a ROWSET element (configurable via fmt).

functions.name: SYS_XMLGEN
functions.doc: Converts a scalar, object type or XMLType value into an XML document with a ROW (or custom) element.

functions.name: SYSDATE
functions.doc: Current date and time of the database server operating system, as a DATE. Not affected by the session time zone. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: SYSTIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Current server date and time with fractional seconds and the OS time zone, as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

functions.name: TABLE
functions.doc: Table collection expression: treats a nested table, varray or pipelined function result as rows in the FROM clause, e.g. FROM TABLE(my_func()).

functions.name: TAN
functions.doc: Tangent of n, where n is an angle in radians.

functions.name: TANH
functions.doc: Hyperbolic tangent of n.

functions.name: TIMESTAMP_TO_SCN
functions.doc: Approximate system change number for a timestamp; useful for flashback queries (AS OF SCN).

functions.name: TO_APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.doc: Converts a detail BLOB from APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT_DETAIL/_AGG into a numeric approximate distinct count.

functions.name: TO_APPROX_PERCENTILE

params: datatype VARCHAR2 ('NUMBER'|'BINARY_FLOAT'|'BINARY_DOUBLE'|'DATE'|'TIMESTAMP'|'INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH'|'INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND')

functions.doc: Computes a percentile value from a detail BLOB produced by APPROX_PERCENTILE_DETAIL or _AGG.

functions.name: TO_BINARY_DOUBLE
functions.doc: Converts a number or string to BINARY_DOUBLE. Strings like 'INF' and 'NaN' are recognised. fmt/nlsparam apply to strings.

functions.name: TO_BINARY_FLOAT
functions.doc: Converts a number or string to single-precision BINARY_FLOAT, possibly losing precision.

functions.name: TO_BLOB

signatures.doc: 12.2+: reads the file contents into a BLOB.

functions.doc: Converts a RAW, LONG RAW or (since 12.2) BFILE value to BLOB.

functions.name: TO_BOOLEAN
functions.doc: Converts a string ('TRUE','yes','on','1'...) or number (0 is FALSE, nonzero TRUE) to the SQL BOOLEAN type.

functions.name: TO_CHAR

signatures.doc: Number to string, e.g. TO_CHAR(1234.5, 'FM9G999D00'). nlsparam sets NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS, NLS_CURRENCY, etc.
Date/timestamp/interval to string, e.g. TO_CHAR(SYSDATE, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'). nlsparam may set NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE.
Converts NCHAR, NVARCHAR2, CLOB or NCLOB data to the database character set.
12.2+: converts BFILE/BLOB bytes using character set ID csid.

functions.doc: Converts a number, datetime, interval or national/LOB text to VARCHAR2, optionally using a format model. Defaults come from NLS_* session settings.

functions.name: TO_CLOB

signatures.doc: 12.2+: converts binary content using character set ID csid.

functions.doc: Converts NCLOB, character data or (since 12.2) BFILE/BLOB content to a CLOB.

functions.name: TO_DATE

signatures.doc: Uses NLS_DATE_FORMAT.
Explicit format model, e.g. TO_DATE('2024-01-31', 'YYYY-MM-DD'); nlsparam like 'NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE = American'.

functions.doc: Converts a string to DATE using a format model (default NLS_DATE_FORMAT). Since 12.2 DEFAULT value ON CONVERSION ERROR returns a fallback instead of raising an error.

functions.name: TO_DSINTERVAL
functions.doc: Converts a string such as '2 10:30:00' or ISO 8601 'P2DT10H30M' to INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND.

functions.name: TO_LOB
functions.doc: Converts a LONG or LONG RAW column to CLOB/NCLOB/BLOB. Allowed only in the select list of a subquery in INSERT or CREATE TABLE AS SELECT.

functions.name: TO_MULTI_BYTE
functions.doc: Converts single-byte characters to their multibyte equivalents where the character set has them.

functions.name: TO_NCHAR

signatures.doc: Character data to the national character set.
Datetime or interval to national-charset string.
Number to national-charset string.

functions.doc: Like TO_CHAR but the result is in the national character set (NVARCHAR2).

functions.name: TO_NCLOB
functions.doc: Converts CLOB data or character strings to NCLOB in the national character set.

functions.name: TO_NUMBER
functions.doc: Converts a string (or binary float) to NUMBER, optionally with a format model like '9G999D99'. Since 12.2 DEFAULT ... ON CONVERSION ERROR avoids ORA-01722.

functions.name: TO_SINGLE_BYTE
functions.doc: Converts multibyte characters to their single-byte equivalents where they exist.

functions.name: TO_TIMESTAMP
functions.doc: Converts a string to TIMESTAMP using fmt (default NLS_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT). Since 12.2 a DEFAULT ... ON CONVERSION ERROR clause can replace errors.

functions.name: TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ
functions.doc: Converts a string to TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE using fmt (default NLS_TIMESTAMP_TZ_FORMAT); TZH, TZM, TZR elements parse the zone.

functions.name: TO_UTC_TIMESTAMP_TZ
functions.doc: Parses an ISO 8601 date/timestamp string (as used in JSON) and returns it normalized to UTC as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.

functions.name: TO_VECTOR
functions.doc: Converts a textual vector such as '[1.5, 2, 3]' (or a VECTOR) to the VECTOR type with optional dimension count and format.

functions.name: TO_YMINTERVAL
functions.doc: Converts a string such as '1-6' or ISO 8601 'P1Y6M' to INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH.

functions.name: TRANSLATE

signatures.doc: Character-by-character mapping; characters in from_string without a counterpart in to_string are removed.
TRANSLATE ... USING converts text between the database and national character sets.

functions.doc: Maps each character of from_string to the matching position in to_string. If to_string is NULL, the result is NULL. The USING form converts character sets.

functions.name: TREAT
functions.doc: Changes the declared type of an expression to a subtype (NULL if it is not one), or with AS JSON marks text as JSON data.

functions.name: TRIM

signatures.doc: Removes leading and trailing blanks.
Removes trim_character (a single character, default blank) from the chosen side(s); BOTH is the default.

functions.doc: Removes leading and/or trailing characters (blank by default) from a string. trim_character must be a single character. Returns NULL if either input is NULL.

functions.name: TRUNC

signatures.doc: Truncates n1 to n2 decimal places (negative n2 zeroes digits left of the point). Default 0.
Truncates a date to the unit in fmt (e.g. YYYY, Q, MM, IW, DD, HH24, MI). Default DD removes the time.

functions.doc: Truncates a number to a number of decimal places, or a datetime down to a format unit (TRUNC(SYSDATE) gives midnight today).

functions.name: TZ_OFFSET
functions.doc: Returns the UTC offset (e.g. '-07:00') for a time zone region name, an offset, or the session/database zone, as of the current date.

functions.name: UID
functions.doc: Integer ID of the session user. Written without parentheses.

functions.name: UNISTR
functions.doc: Interprets \xxxx UTF-16 escapes in string and returns national-charset text, e.g. UNISTR('caf\00e9'). Use \\ for a literal backslash.

functions.name: UPDATEXML
functions.doc: Replaces the nodes matched by each XPath with the given values. Deprecated: use XQuery Update (copy/modify/return).

functions.name: UPPER
functions.doc: Returns char with all letters in upper case.

functions.name: USER
functions.doc: Name of the session user. Written without parentheses; in a definer-rights unit it still returns the session user.

functions.name: USERENV
functions.doc: Legacy session information lookup (e.g. 'LANGUAGE', 'SESSIONID'). Deprecated: use SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', ...).

functions.name: VALIDATE_CONVERSION
functions.doc: Returns 1 if expr can be converted to type_name (e.g. NUMBER, DATE, TIMESTAMP), 0 if not. NULL input returns 1.

functions.name: VALUE
functions.doc: Returns the object instance stored in a row of an object table, given its table alias.

functions.name: VAR_POP
functions.doc: Population variance of the non-NULL values. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: VAR_SAMP
functions.doc: Sample variance; NULL for a single-row group. Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: VARIANCE
functions.doc: Sample variance, but returns 0 for a single-row group (unlike VAR_SAMP). Also usable as an analytic function with OVER (...).

functions.name: VECTOR
functions.doc: Constructor equivalent to TO_VECTOR: builds a VECTOR value from text.

functions.name: VECTOR_DIMENSION_COUNT
functions.doc: Number of dimensions of a vector.

functions.name: VECTOR_DIMENSION_FORMAT
functions.doc: Storage format of the vector dimensions: INT8, FLOAT32, FLOAT64 or BINARY.

functions.name: VECTOR_DISTANCE
functions.doc: Distance between two vectors under the chosen metric (default COSINE); the core of similarity search ORDER BY ... FETCH APPROX FIRST n ROWS.

functions.name: VECTOR_EMBEDDING

params: model_name IDENTIFIER USING expr AS data

functions.doc: Generates a vector embedding from text or other data using an ONNX embedding model loaded into the database.

functions.name: VECTOR_NORM
functions.doc: Euclidean norm (magnitude) of a vector.

functions.name: VECTOR_SERIALIZE
functions.doc: Synonym of FROM_VECTOR: serializes a vector to text.

functions.name: VERSIONS_ENDSCN
functions.doc: Flashback Version Query pseudocolumn: SCN when the row version expired (NULL if current or deleted row).

functions.name: VERSIONS_ENDTIME
functions.doc: Flashback Version Query pseudocolumn: timestamp when the row version expired.

functions.name: VERSIONS_OPERATION
functions.doc: Flashback Version Query pseudocolumn: I, U or D for the insert, update or delete that created the version.

functions.name: VERSIONS_STARTSCN
functions.doc: Flashback Version Query pseudocolumn: SCN when the row version was created (NULL if before the query range).

functions.name: VERSIONS_STARTTIME
functions.doc: Flashback Version Query pseudocolumn: timestamp when the row version was created.

functions.name: VERSIONS_XID
functions.doc: Flashback Version Query pseudocolumn: ID of the transaction that created the row version.

functions.name: VSIZE
functions.doc: Number of bytes in the internal representation of expr; NULL for NULL.

functions.name: WIDTH_BUCKET
functions.doc: Assigns expr to one of num_buckets equal-width buckets between min_value and max_value. Values below the range get 0; values at or above the top get num_buckets+1.

functions.name: XMLAGG
functions.doc: Concatenates XML fragments from a group into one XMLType, optionally ordered. NULLs are dropped.

functions.name: XMLCAST
functions.doc: Casts an XML value to a SQL scalar type (or an XMLType), e.g. XMLCAST(XMLQUERY(...) AS NUMBER).

functions.name: XMLCDATA
functions.doc: Builds an XML CDATA section from a string; the value must not contain "]]>".

functions.name: XMLCOLATTVAL
functions.doc: Creates a fragment of <column name="...">value</column> elements, one per argument.

functions.name: XMLCOMMENT
functions.doc: Builds an XML comment <!--...-->; the text may not contain two consecutive dashes or end with one.

functions.name: XMLCONCAT
functions.doc: Concatenates XMLType values into one fragment. NULL arguments are skipped.

functions.name: XMLDIFF
functions.doc: Compares two XML documents and returns the differences as an XML diff document usable with XMLPATCH.

functions.name: XMLELEMENT
functions.doc: Creates an XML element with the given name, optional XMLATTRIBUTES(...), and child content, e.g. XMLELEMENT("emp", XMLATTRIBUTES(id AS "id"), name).

functions.name: XMLEXISTS
functions.doc: Condition that is true when an XQuery expression returns a non-empty sequence, e.g. WHERE XMLEXISTS('/a[b=1]' PASSING doc).

functions.name: XMLFOREST
functions.doc: Creates a forest of sibling elements, one per argument, named after the column or alias. NULL values produce no element.

functions.name: XMLISVALID
functions.doc: Returns 1 if the XML instance is valid against the given (or its own) registered XML schema, else 0.

functions.name: XMLPARSE
functions.doc: Parses a string into XMLType as a single DOCUMENT or a CONTENT fragment. WELLFORMED skips well-formedness checks.

functions.name: XMLPATCH
functions.doc: Applies a diff document (as produced by XMLDIFF) to an XML document.

functions.name: XMLPI
functions.doc: Builds an XML processing instruction <?identifier value?>. The name cannot be "xml" in any case.

functions.name: XMLQUERY
functions.doc: Evaluates an XQuery expression and returns the result as XMLType content, e.g. XMLQUERY('/po/item' PASSING doc RETURNING CONTENT).

functions.name: XMLROOT
functions.doc: Adds an XML declaration (version and standalone) to the root of an XML value.

functions.name: XMLSEQUENCE
functions.doc: Splits an XML fragment or cursor rows into a varray of XMLType, typically used with TABLE(). Deprecated: use XMLTABLE.

functions.name: XMLSERIALIZE
functions.doc: Serializes an XMLType to a string or LOB, optionally pretty-printed with INDENT.

functions.name: XMLTABLE

params: [COLUMNS col type PATH 'xpath' [DEFAULT expr] | col FOR ORDINALITY, ...]

functions.doc: Shreds XML into relational rows in the FROM clause: XMLTABLE('/emps/emp' PASSING doc COLUMNS id NUMBER PATH '@id', name VARCHAR2(30) PATH 'name').

functions.name: XMLTRANSFORM
functions.doc: Applies an XSLT stylesheet to an XML instance and returns the transformed XML.

functions.name: XMLTYPE
functions.doc: XMLType constructor: parses a string, CLOB or BLOB (with charset ID) into an XMLType instance, optionally schema-based.

packages.name: DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO
packages.doc: Registers module, action and client info for the session (shown in V$SESSION, V$SQL, AWR) and reports long-running operation progress.

members.name: READ_CLIENT_INFO
members.doc: Reads the CLIENT_INFO value of the current session.

members.name: READ_MODULE
members.doc: Reads the current module and action names.

members.name: SET_ACTION
members.doc: Sets the action name (max 64 bytes) within the current module.

members.name: SET_CLIENT_INFO
members.doc: Sets V$SESSION.CLIENT_INFO (max 64 bytes).

members.name: SET_MODULE
members.doc: Sets the module (max 64 bytes, longer is truncated) and action for the session.

members.name: SET_SESSION_LONGOPS
members.doc: Creates or updates a row in V$SESSION_LONGOPS. Start with rindex => DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO.SET_SESSION_LONGOPS_NOHINT.

packages.name: DBMS_ASSERT
packages.doc: Validates and quotes input used to build dynamic SQL, helping prevent SQL injection.

members.name: ENQUOTE_LITERAL
members.doc: Wraps a string in single quotes, checking that embedded quotes are paired.

members.name: ENQUOTE_NAME
members.doc: Wraps a name in double quotes (upper-casing it unless capitalize is FALSE).

members.name: NOOP
members.doc: Returns the input unchanged; documents that a value was deliberately not checked.

members.name: QUALIFIED_SQL_NAME
members.doc: Verifies the input is a valid qualified SQL name (schema.object@dblink); raises ORA-44004 otherwise.

members.name: SCHEMA_NAME
members.doc: Verifies the input names an existing schema; raises ORA-44001 otherwise.

members.name: SIMPLE_SQL_NAME
members.doc: Verifies the input is a simple SQL name (identifier or quoted identifier); raises ORA-44003 otherwise.

members.name: SQL_OBJECT_NAME
members.doc: Verifies the input is the qualified name of an existing object; raises ORA-44002 otherwise.

packages.name: DBMS_CRYPTO
packages.doc: Cryptographic hashing, MACs, symmetric encryption/decryption (AES, 3DES...) and secure random values. Algorithm constants like DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH_SH256 select the method.

members.name: DECRYPT

signatures.doc: Procedure overload writing into a LOB.

members.doc: Decrypts RAW data with the same typ (cipher + chaining + padding, e.g. ENCRYPT_AES256 + CHAIN_CBC + PAD_PKCS5), key and IV used to encrypt.

members.name: ENCRYPT

signatures.doc: Procedure overload for LOB input.

members.doc: Encrypts RAW data. Convert text with UTL_I18N.STRING_TO_RAW first. typ combines cipher, chaining and padding constants.

members.name: HASH

params: src IN CLOB CHARACTER SET ANY_CS

members.doc: Cryptographic hash of the input; typ is HASH_MD5, HASH_SH1, HASH_SH256, HASH_SH384 or HASH_SH512.

members.name: MAC

params: src IN CLOB CHARACTER SET ANY_CS

members.doc: Keyed hash (HMAC) of the input; typ is HMAC_MD5, HMAC_SH1, HMAC_SH256, HMAC_SH384 or HMAC_SH512.

members.name: RANDOMBYTES
members.doc: Cryptographically secure random bytes, e.g. for keys and IVs (max 4096 bytes).

members.name: RANDOMINTEGER
members.doc: Cryptographically secure random integer.

members.name: RANDOMNUMBER
members.doc: Cryptographically secure random 128-bit integer as a NUMBER.

packages.name: DBMS_JOB
packages.doc: Legacy job queue. Deprecated: use DBMS_SCHEDULER. Since 19c, DBMS_JOB jobs are implemented as Scheduler jobs and SUBMIT needs a COMMIT to take effect.

members.name: BROKEN
members.doc: Marks a job as broken (not run) or not broken.

members.name: CHANGE
members.doc: Changes the action, next run date and interval of a job; NULL leaves a value unchanged.

members.name: INTERVAL
members.doc: Changes the interval expression, a string evaluated to the next date such as 'SYSDATE + 1/24'.

members.name: NEXT_DATE
members.doc: Changes when the job next runs.

members.name: REMOVE
members.doc: Removes a job from the queue (does not stop a running execution).

members.name: RUN
members.doc: Runs a job immediately in the current session, even if broken.

members.name: SUBMIT
members.doc: Submits a PL/SQL block (what, ending in ';') as a job; returns its job number. COMMIT to activate.

members.name: WHAT
members.doc: Changes the PL/SQL the job runs.

packages.name: DBMS_LOB
packages.doc: Operations on BLOB, CLOB, NCLOB and BFILE locators: reading, writing, comparing, searching, temporary LOBs and loading from files.

members.name: APPEND
members.doc: Appends the whole source LOB to the end of the destination LOB.

members.name: CLOSE
members.doc: Closes a LOB previously opened with OPEN.

members.name: COMPARE
members.doc: Compares two LOBs of the same type; returns 0 if equal, nonzero otherwise, NULL for invalid arguments.

members.name: CONVERTTOBLOB
members.doc: Converts character data to binary in blob_csid charset (DBMS_LOB.DEFAULT_CSID); start lang_context at DEFAULT_LANG_CTX.

members.name: CONVERTTOCLOB
members.doc: Converts binary data in charset blob_csid into a CLOB. Offsets are advanced past the converted data.

members.name: COPY
members.doc: Copies amount bytes/characters from the source LOB into the destination at the given offsets.

members.name: CREATETEMPORARY
members.doc: Creates a temporary LOB in the temporary tablespace; dur is DBMS_LOB.SESSION or DBMS_LOB.CALL. Free it with FREETEMPORARY.

members.name: ERASE
members.doc: Erases part of a LOB, filling with zero bytes (BLOB) or spaces (CLOB); amount returns what was erased.

members.name: FILECLOSE
members.doc: Closes a BFILE opened with FILEOPEN or OPEN.

members.name: FILECLOSEALL
members.doc: Closes all BFILEs opened in the session.

members.name: FILEEXISTS
members.doc: Returns 1 if the operating-system file behind a BFILE exists, otherwise 0.

members.name: FILEGETNAME
members.doc: Returns the directory object name and file name of a BFILE locator.

members.name: FILEISOPEN
members.doc: Returns 1 if the BFILE is open, otherwise 0.

members.name: FILEOPEN
members.doc: Opens a BFILE for read-only access.

members.name: FREETEMPORARY
members.doc: Frees a temporary LOB and its space.

members.name: GETCHUNKSIZE
members.doc: Returns the usable chunk size of a LOB; writes in multiples of it are most efficient.

members.name: GETLENGTH
members.doc: Length of a LOB in bytes (BLOB/BFILE) or characters (CLOB). NULL for a NULL locator, 0 for an empty LOB.

members.name: INSTR
members.doc: Position of the nth occurrence of pattern in the LOB starting at offset; 0 if not found.

members.name: ISOPEN
members.doc: Returns 1 if the LOB was opened with OPEN, otherwise 0.

members.name: ISTEMPORARY
members.doc: Returns 1 if the locator refers to a temporary LOB, otherwise 0.

members.name: LOADBLOBFROMFILE
members.doc: Loads BFILE content into a BLOB; offsets return positions after the load. Use DBMS_LOB.LOBMAXSIZE for the whole file.

members.name: LOADCLOBFROMFILE
members.doc: Loads BFILE text into a CLOB, converting from bfile_csid (DBMS_LOB.DEFAULT_CSID for the database charset).

members.name: LOADFROMFILE
members.doc: Copies raw BFILE bytes into a LOB without charset conversion. Deprecated in favor of LOADBLOBFROMFILE/LOADCLOBFROMFILE.

members.name: OPEN
members.doc: Opens a LOB in DBMS_LOB.LOB_READONLY or LOB_READWRITE mode, deferring index updates until CLOSE.

members.name: READ
members.doc: Reads up to amount bytes/characters from offset into buffer; amount returns the count read. Raises NO_DATA_FOUND at end of LOB.

members.name: SUBSTR
members.doc: Returns amount bytes (RAW) or characters (VARCHAR2) of a LOB starting at offset. Note the argument order: amount before offset.

members.name: TRIM
members.doc: Shortens a LOB to newlen bytes/characters.

members.name: WRITE
members.doc: Writes amount bytes/characters from buffer into the LOB at offset, overwriting existing data.

members.name: WRITEAPPEND
members.doc: Appends amount bytes/characters from buffer to the end of the LOB.

packages.name: DBMS_LOCK
packages.doc: User-defined locks via the Oracle lock manager (UL enqueues), for serializing application work across sessions. SLEEP lives here historically.

members.name: ALLOCATE_UNIQUE
members.doc: Maps a lock name to a lock handle for use with REQUEST/CONVERT/RELEASE. Performs a COMMIT.

members.name: CONVERT
members.doc: Changes the mode of a held lock; returns 0 success, 1 timeout, 2 deadlock, 3 parameter error, 4 not owned, 5 illegal handle.

members.name: RELEASE
members.doc: Releases a lock; returns 0 success, 3 parameter error, 4 lock not owned, 5 illegal handle.

members.name: REQUEST
members.doc: Requests a lock in a mode (NL, SS, SX, S, SSX, X); returns 0 success, 1 timeout, 2 deadlock, 3 param error, 4 already owned, 5 bad handle.

members.name: SLEEP
members.doc: Suspends the session for the given seconds (hundredths allowed). Deprecated since 18c: use DBMS_SESSION.SLEEP.

packages.name: DBMS_METADATA
packages.doc: Extracts object metadata as DDL or XML. Use DBMS_METADATA.SESSION_TRANSFORM (-1) with SET_TRANSFORM_PARAM to configure GET_DDL output for the session (e.g. 'SQLTERMINATOR', 'STORAGE').

members.name: ADD_TRANSFORM
members.doc: Adds a transform (e.g. 'DDL') to an OPEN handle; returns a transform handle for SET_TRANSFORM_PARAM.

members.name: CLOSE
members.doc: Releases resources for a handle opened with OPEN.

members.name: FETCH_CLOB
members.doc: Fetches the next object metadata as a CLOB; returns NULL when no more objects match.

members.name: FETCH_DDL
members.doc: Fetches the next object as a collection of DDL statements.

members.name: GET_DDL
members.doc: Returns the DDL to recreate an object, e.g. GET_DDL('TABLE', 'EMP', 'HR'). Names are case-sensitive; use 'PACKAGE_BODY' style types.

members.name: GET_DEPENDENT_DDL
members.doc: DDL for objects that depend on a base object, e.g. object_type 'INDEX', 'TRIGGER', 'OBJECT_GRANT' for a table.

members.name: GET_GRANTED_DDL
members.doc: DDL for grants given to a user or role: 'SYSTEM_GRANT', 'ROLE_GRANT', 'OBJECT_GRANT', 'DEFAULT_ROLE'.

members.name: GET_XML
members.doc: Returns the object metadata as XML.

members.name: OPEN
members.doc: Starts a programmatic metadata retrieval for an object type; returns a handle for SET_FILTER, ADD_TRANSFORM and FETCH_*.

members.name: SET_FILTER
members.doc: Restricts which objects are retrieved, e.g. SET_FILTER(h, 'SCHEMA', 'HR') or 'NAME', 'NAME_EXPR'.

members.name: SET_TRANSFORM_PARAM
members.doc: Sets a transform option. Pass DBMS_METADATA.SESSION_TRANSFORM to affect GET_DDL, e.g. ('SEGMENT_ATTRIBUTES', FALSE).

packages.name: DBMS_OUTPUT
packages.doc: Buffers text lines from PL/SQL so clients (SQL*Plus SET SERVEROUTPUT ON, IDEs) can display them after the call completes.

members.name: ENABLE
members.doc: Enables buffering. NULL buffer_size means unlimited (recommended); otherwise 2000 to 1000000 bytes.

members.name: DISABLE
members.doc: Disables output and discards the buffer contents.

members.name: PUT
members.doc: Appends text to the current line without a newline.

members.name: PUT_LINE
members.doc: Writes a line to the buffer (max 32767 bytes per line). Output is shown only after the block finishes.

members.name: NEW_LINE
members.doc: Ends the current line started with PUT.

members.name: GET_LINE
members.doc: Reads one buffered line; status is 0 on success, 1 when no more lines.

members.name: GET_LINES
members.doc: Reads up to numlines buffered lines into an array; numlines returns the count read.

packages.name: DBMS_RANDOM
packages.doc: Pseudo-random number and string generator. Not suitable for cryptography; use DBMS_CRYPTO.RANDOMBYTES for that.

members.name: INITIALIZE
members.doc: Seeds the generator. Deprecated: use SEED.

members.name: NORMAL
members.doc: Random number from a standard normal distribution (mean 0, standard deviation 1).

members.name: RANDOM
members.doc: Random integer in [-2^31, 2^31). Deprecated: use VALUE.

members.name: SEED
members.doc: Resets the seed so the following sequence is repeatable.

members.name: STRING
members.doc: Random string of len characters; opt is 'U' upper, 'L' lower, 'A' mixed alpha, 'X' upper alphanumeric, 'P' any printable.

members.name: TERMINATE
members.doc: No-op kept for compatibility. Deprecated.

members.name: VALUE

signatures.doc: Returns 0 <= x < 1.
Returns low <= x < high.

members.doc: Random decimal number with 38 digits of precision, in [0,1) or in [low,high). Use TRUNC for integers.

packages.name: DBMS_SCHEDULER
packages.doc: The Oracle Scheduler: create and manage jobs, programs, schedules, windows and chains. Successor to DBMS_JOB.

members.name: CREATE_JOB

params: [start_date IN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NULL]
[end_date IN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NULL]
[start_date IN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NULL]
[end_date IN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NULL]

members.doc: Creates a job: inline action, named program and/or named schedule. repeat_interval uses calendar syntax like 'FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=2'. Jobs are disabled unless enabled => TRUE.

members.name: CREATE_PROGRAM
members.doc: Creates a reusable program (what to run) that jobs can reference.

members.name: CREATE_SCHEDULE

params: [start_date IN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NULL]
[end_date IN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NULL]

members.doc: Creates a named, reusable schedule (when to run).

members.name: DISABLE
members.doc: Disables one or more (comma-separated) jobs, programs, chains or windows.

members.name: DROP_JOB
members.doc: Drops one or more jobs; force TRUE stops a running instance first.

members.name: DROP_PROGRAM
members.doc: Drops a program; force TRUE disables jobs that reference it.

members.name: DROP_SCHEDULE
members.doc: Drops a schedule; force TRUE disables jobs and windows using it.

members.name: ENABLE
members.doc: Enables one or more (comma-separated) jobs, programs, chains or windows.

members.name: RUN_JOB
members.doc: Runs a job immediately; with use_current_session TRUE it runs synchronously in the calling session.

members.name: SET_ATTRIBUTE

params: value IN VARCHAR2|NUMBER|BOOLEAN|DATE|TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE|INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND

members.doc: Changes an attribute of a scheduler object, e.g. SET_ATTRIBUTE('MY_JOB', 'repeat_interval', 'FREQ=HOURLY').

members.name: SET_JOB_ARGUMENT_VALUE
members.doc: Sets the value of a job argument by position or name.

members.name: STOP_JOB
members.doc: Stops a running job; force TRUE kills the job slave (requires MANAGE SCHEDULER).

packages.name: DBMS_SESSION
packages.doc: Session-level settings: roles, NLS parameters, application contexts, client identifiers, package state and sleeping.

members.name: CLEAR_CONTEXT
members.doc: Clears one attribute, or all attributes, of an application context. Must be called from the package bound to the context.

members.name: CLEAR_IDENTIFIER
members.doc: Removes the client identifier set with SET_IDENTIFIER.

members.name: IS_ROLE_ENABLED
members.doc: TRUE if the named role is currently enabled in the session.

members.name: IS_SESSION_ALIVE
members.doc: TRUE if the session with the given UNIQUE_SESSION_ID value still exists.

members.name: MODIFY_PACKAGE_STATE
members.doc: Frees or reinitializes package state: DBMS_SESSION.FREE_ALL_RESOURCES or DBMS_SESSION.REINITIALIZE.

members.name: RESET_PACKAGE
members.doc: Discards the state of all packages in the session (variables reset). Takes effect after the current call completes.

members.name: SESSION_TRACE_DISABLE
members.doc: Disables SQL trace for the current session.

members.name: SESSION_TRACE_ENABLE
members.doc: Enables SQL trace for the current session, optionally including waits, binds and plan statistics.

members.name: SET_CONTEXT
members.doc: Sets an application context attribute readable via SYS_CONTEXT. Only callable from the trusted package named in CREATE CONTEXT.

members.name: SET_IDENTIFIER
members.doc: Sets CLIENT_IDENTIFIER for the session (max 64 bytes), visible in V$SESSION and audit trails.

members.name: SET_NLS
members.doc: Equivalent to ALTER SESSION SET param = value; quote string values, e.g. SET_NLS('NLS_DATE_FORMAT', '''YYYY-MM-DD''').

members.name: SET_ROLE
members.doc: Equivalent to SET ROLE role_cmd, e.g. SET_ROLE('hr_role IDENTIFIED BY pwd'). Not allowed in definer-rights units.

members.name: SLEEP
members.doc: Suspends the session for the given number of seconds (fractions allowed). Replaces DBMS_LOCK.SLEEP; no extra grant needed.

members.name: UNIQUE_SESSION_ID
members.doc: Returns an identifier unique among currently connected sessions (up to 24 bytes).

packages.name: DBMS_SQL
packages.doc: Low-level dynamic SQL: parse, bind, describe, execute and fetch statements whose structure is unknown until run time. Convertible to and from REF CURSORs.

members.name: BIND_ARRAY
members.doc: Binds a PL/SQL index-by table to a placeholder for array (bulk) DML.

members.name: BIND_VARIABLE
members.doc: Binds a value to a placeholder such as ':id' in a parsed statement. out_value_size sizes VARCHAR2 OUT binds.

members.name: CLOSE_CURSOR
members.doc: Closes the cursor and sets c to NULL.

members.name: COLUMN_VALUE
members.doc: Retrieves the value of a defined column for the current fetched row.

members.name: DEFINE_ARRAY
members.doc: Defines a collection to receive cnt rows per fetch for a select-list column.

members.name: DEFINE_COLUMN
members.doc: Declares the type of the select-list column at position; VARCHAR2 columns need column_size.

members.name: DESCRIBE_COLUMNS
members.doc: Describes the select-list columns of a parsed query. Column names are limited to 32 bytes; prefer DESCRIBE_COLUMNS2.

members.name: DESCRIBE_COLUMNS2
members.doc: Like DESCRIBE_COLUMNS but supports long column names.

members.name: DESCRIBE_COLUMNS3
members.doc: Like DESCRIBE_COLUMNS2 and also returns user-defined type names.

members.name: EXECUTE
members.doc: Executes the parsed statement; returns rows processed for DML (ignore for queries).

members.name: EXECUTE_AND_FETCH
members.doc: Executes and fetches the first row in one call. exact TRUE raises an error unless exactly one row matches.

members.name: FETCH_ROWS
members.doc: Fetches the next row (or array batch); returns the number fetched, 0 when exhausted.

members.name: GET_NEXT_RESULT
members.doc: Retrieves the next implicit result set returned by a called procedure via RETURN_RESULT.

members.name: IS_OPEN
members.doc: TRUE if the cursor number refers to an open DBMS_SQL cursor.

members.name: LAST_ERROR_POSITION
members.doc: Byte offset in the statement text where the last parse error occurred. Call immediately after the failing PARSE.

members.name: LAST_ROW_COUNT
members.doc: Cumulative count of rows fetched by the last FETCH_ROWS or EXECUTE_AND_FETCH call.

members.name: OPEN_CURSOR
members.doc: Opens a new cursor and returns its ID. security_level 1 or 2 restricts use to the same user/role environment.

members.name: PARSE
members.doc: Parses a statement (use DBMS_SQL.NATIVE for language_flag). DDL is executed immediately on parse.

members.name: RETURN_RESULT
members.doc: Returns an open cursor as an implicit result set to the client or immediate caller.

members.name: TO_CURSOR_NUMBER
members.doc: Converts an opened REF CURSOR into a DBMS_SQL cursor number (e.g. to describe its columns).

members.name: TO_REFCURSOR
members.doc: Converts an executed DBMS_SQL cursor into a REF CURSOR; the cursor number becomes unusable.

members.name: VARIABLE_VALUE
members.doc: Retrieves the value of an OUT bind variable (e.g. from RETURNING INTO or an anonymous block).

packages.name: DBMS_STATS
packages.doc: Gathers, deletes, locks, exports and imports optimizer statistics, and manages statistics preferences.

members.name: CREATE_STAT_TABLE
members.doc: Creates a user table to hold exported statistics.

members.name: DELETE_SCHEMA_STATS
members.doc: Deletes statistics for all objects in a schema.

members.name: DELETE_TABLE_STATS
members.doc: Deletes table statistics, by default also column, index and partition statistics.

members.name: EXPORT_TABLE_STATS
members.doc: Copies a table's statistics into a stat table created with CREATE_STAT_TABLE.

members.name: GATHER_DATABASE_STATS

params: [method_opt IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT 'FOR ALL COLUMNS SIZE AUTO']

members.doc: Gathers statistics for all objects in the database. options: GATHER, GATHER AUTO, GATHER STALE, GATHER EMPTY, LIST *.

members.name: GATHER_INDEX_STATS
members.doc: Gathers statistics for an index (indexes are also covered by table gathering with cascade).

members.name: GATHER_SCHEMA_STATS

params: [method_opt IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT 'FOR ALL COLUMNS SIZE AUTO']

members.doc: Gathers statistics for all objects in a schema. options 'GATHER STALE' or 'GATHER AUTO' limit work to objects that need it.

members.name: GATHER_TABLE_STATS

params: [method_opt IN VARCHAR2 DEFAULT 'FOR ALL COLUMNS SIZE AUTO']

members.doc: Gathers table, column and (with cascade) index statistics. Defaults come from table preferences, e.g. GATHER_TABLE_STATS('HR', 'EMP').

members.name: GET_PREFS
members.doc: Returns the effective value of a statistics preference (e.g. 'STALE_PERCENT', 'METHOD_OPT') for a table or globally.

members.name: IMPORT_TABLE_STATS
members.doc: Loads table statistics from a stat table into the dictionary.

members.name: LOCK_TABLE_STATS
members.doc: Locks a table's statistics so gathering jobs leave them unchanged (force => TRUE overrides).

members.name: SET_GLOBAL_PREFS
members.doc: Sets a global default statistics preference.

members.name: SET_TABLE_PREFS
members.doc: Sets a statistics preference for one table, e.g. ('HR', 'EMP', 'INCREMENTAL', 'TRUE').

members.name: UNLOCK_TABLE_STATS
members.doc: Unlocks statistics previously locked with LOCK_TABLE_STATS.

packages.name: DBMS_UTILITY
packages.doc: Assorted utility routines: error and call stack formatting, timing, name resolution, list conversion, schema compilation and hashing.

members.name: COMMA_TO_TABLE
members.doc: Splits a comma-separated list of names into a PL/SQL table. Elements must be valid identifiers (not arbitrary text).

members.name: COMPILE_SCHEMA
members.doc: Recompiles procedures, functions, packages, types and triggers in a schema; compile_all FALSE compiles only invalid ones.

members.name: DB_VERSION
members.doc: Returns the database version string and the COMPATIBLE parameter setting.

members.name: EXPAND_SQL_TEXT
members.doc: Rewrites a query with all views expanded into their underlying base-table SQL.

members.name: FORMAT_CALL_STACK
members.doc: Current PL/SQL call stack as text (object handles, line numbers, names).

members.name: FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE
members.doc: Backtrace from the point the current exception was raised, with line numbers. Call in an exception handler.

members.name: FORMAT_ERROR_STACK
members.doc: Current error stack (up to 2000 bytes), more complete than SQLERRM.

members.name: GET_CPU_TIME
