members.doc: CPU time used by the session in hundredths of a second; use differences between calls.

members.name: GET_HASH_VALUE
members.doc: Hash of name in the range base .. base + hash_size - 1. hash_size should be a power of 2.

members.name: GET_TIME
members.doc: Elapsed time in hundredths of a second from an arbitrary epoch; subtract two calls to time code.

members.name: IS_CLUSTER_DATABASE
members.doc: TRUE if the database runs in Real Application Clusters mode.

members.name: NAME_RESOLVE
members.doc: Resolves a (possibly synonym-based) name to schema, object, sub-object and dblink. context 1 is for PL/SQL units, 2 for tables.

members.name: NAME_TOKENIZE
members.doc: Parses a name of the form a[.b[.c]][@dblink] into its parts without resolving it.

members.name: TABLE_TO_COMMA
members.doc: Joins a PL/SQL table of names into a comma-separated list.

packages.name: DBMS_XPLAN
packages.doc: Formats execution plans from PLAN_TABLE, the cursor cache, AWR and SQL plan baselines. Query with SELECT * FROM TABLE(DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY_CURSOR(...)).

members.name: DISPLAY
members.doc: Shows the plan produced by EXPLAIN PLAN. format: BASIC, TYPICAL, SERIAL, ALL, plus modifiers like '+OUTLINE -BYTES'.

members.name: DISPLAY_AWR
members.doc: Shows plans stored in the Automatic Workload Repository for a SQL_ID. Deprecated in 12.2+: use DISPLAY_WORKLOAD_REPOSITORY.

members.name: DISPLAY_CURSOR
members.doc: Shows the actual plan of a cached cursor (default: last statement of the session). Use format 'ALLSTATS LAST' with GATHER_PLAN_STATISTICS for row-source stats.

members.name: DISPLAY_SQL_PLAN_BASELINE
members.doc: Shows plans stored in SQL plan baselines.

members.name: DISPLAY_WORKLOAD_REPOSITORY
members.doc: Shows AWR-stored plans for a SQL_ID, with multitenant awareness. Replaces DISPLAY_AWR.

packages.name: UTL_FILE
packages.doc: Reads and writes operating-system text and binary files on the database server, through directory objects.

members.name: FCLOSE
members.doc: Closes an open file handle, flushing pending writes.

members.name: FCLOSE_ALL
members.doc: Closes all file handles opened in the session (handles are not reset; IS_OPEN still returns TRUE).

members.name: FCOPY
members.doc: Copies a text file, or a range of its lines, to a new file.

members.name: FFLUSH
members.doc: Writes buffered data for the file to disk.

members.name: FGETATTR
members.doc: Reports whether a file exists, its length in bytes and its block size.

members.name: FOPEN
members.doc: Opens a file in a directory object (name in upper case) and returns a handle. max_linesize can be up to 32767.

members.name: FOPEN_NCHAR
members.doc: Opens a file for Unicode (UTF-8) reading/writing with the *_NCHAR procedures.

members.name: FREMOVE
members.doc: Deletes a file from a directory object.

members.name: FRENAME
members.doc: Renames or moves a file.

members.name: GET_LINE
members.doc: Reads one line (without the terminator) into buffer. Raises NO_DATA_FOUND at end of file.

members.name: GET_RAW
members.doc: Reads binary data from a file opened in byte mode.

members.name: IS_OPEN
members.doc: TRUE if the handle refers to an open file.

members.name: NEW_LINE
members.doc: Writes one or more line terminators.

members.name: PUT
members.doc: Writes text without a line terminator.

members.name: PUT_LINE
members.doc: Writes text followed by a platform line terminator.

members.name: PUT_RAW
members.doc: Writes binary data to a file opened in byte mode.

members.name: PUTF
members.doc: Formatted write: %s in format is replaced by the next argument and \n by a line terminator.

packages.name: UTL_HTTP
packages.doc: Makes HTTP(S) calls from the database. Needs a network ACL (DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN) and, for HTTPS, a wallet. Always END_RESPONSE to free connections.

members.name: BEGIN_REQUEST
members.doc: Starts a request (sends the request line); follow with SET_HEADER, WRITE_TEXT and GET_RESPONSE.

members.name: END_REQUEST
members.doc: Ends a request without reading a response.

members.name: END_RESPONSE
members.doc: Ends the response and releases the connection. Call it even after errors to avoid exhausting connections.

members.name: GET_HEADER
members.doc: Returns the nth response header name and value.

members.name: GET_HEADER_COUNT
members.doc: Number of headers in the response.

members.name: GET_RESPONSE
members.doc: Completes the request and reads the status line and headers; the RESP record has status_code and reason_phrase.

members.name: READ_LINE

params: data OUT NOCOPY VARCHAR2 CHARACTER SET ANY_CS

members.doc: Reads one line of the response body. Raises UTL_HTTP.END_OF_BODY when the body is exhausted.

members.name: READ_RAW
members.doc: Reads binary response body data. Raises END_OF_BODY at the end.

members.name: READ_TEXT

params: data OUT NOCOPY VARCHAR2 CHARACTER SET ANY_CS

members.doc: Reads response body text (up to len characters). Raises UTL_HTTP.END_OF_BODY when done; loop until then.

members.name: REQUEST
members.doc: Simple GET returning at most the first 2000 bytes of the response body. Usable in SQL.

members.name: REQUEST_PIECES
members.doc: Simple GET returning the body as a table of 2000-byte pieces.

members.name: SET_BODY_CHARSET
members.doc: Sets the default character set for request/response bodies whose Content-Type lacks one.

members.name: SET_HEADER
members.doc: Adds a request header, e.g. SET_HEADER(req, 'Content-Type', 'application/json').

members.name: SET_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT
members.doc: Sets the default network read timeout in seconds for subsequent requests.

members.name: SET_WALLET
members.doc: Sets the Oracle wallet (e.g. 'file:/path/to/wallet') used for HTTPS requests.

members.name: WRITE_RAW
members.doc: Writes binary data to the request body.

members.name: WRITE_TEXT

params: data IN VARCHAR2 CHARACTER SET ANY_CS

members.doc: Writes text to the request body; set Content-Length or chunked Transfer-Encoding beforehand.

packages.name: UTL_RAW
packages.doc: Functions for manipulating RAW (binary) data: casting, concatenation, slicing, bitwise operations and comparison.

members.name: BIT_AND
members.doc: Bitwise AND of two RAW values; the shorter is extended with the longer value's remaining bytes.

members.name: BIT_COMPLEMENT
members.doc: Bitwise NOT of a RAW value.

members.name: BIT_OR
members.doc: Bitwise OR of two RAW values.

members.name: BIT_XOR
members.doc: Bitwise XOR of two RAW values.

members.name: CAST_FROM_BINARY_INTEGER
members.doc: Returns the 4-byte binary representation of an integer.

members.name: CAST_FROM_NUMBER
members.doc: Returns the internal Oracle NUMBER representation as RAW.

members.name: CAST_TO_BINARY_INTEGER
members.doc: Interprets a 1-4 byte RAW as a binary integer.

members.name: CAST_TO_NUMBER
members.doc: Interprets a RAW holding an Oracle NUMBER internal representation as a NUMBER.

members.name: CAST_TO_RAW
members.doc: Reinterprets the bytes of a VARCHAR2 as RAW without any conversion.

members.name: CAST_TO_VARCHAR2
members.doc: Reinterprets RAW bytes as a VARCHAR2 in the database character set, without conversion.

members.name: COMPARE
members.doc: Returns 0 if the RAWs are identical, otherwise the 1-based position of the first differing byte. The shorter is padded with pad.

members.name: CONCAT
members.doc: Concatenates up to 12 RAW values (result max 32767 bytes).

members.name: CONVERT
members.doc: Converts RAW text bytes between character sets, given as NLS_LANG-style names such as 'AMERICAN_AMERICA.AL32UTF8'.

members.name: COPIES
members.doc: Returns r repeated n times.

members.name: LENGTH
members.doc: Number of bytes in a RAW value.

members.name: REVERSE
members.doc: Reverses the byte order of a RAW value.

members.name: SUBSTR
members.doc: Returns len bytes of r starting at pos (negative pos counts from the end).
